source: The ACME example template docs/reference/examples/acme/templates/review-design-system.yaml. The JSON was drafted by hand and checked against the file. A template is a Section with no source (section template schema, README).

name: minimal
source: Hand-written. Section template schema, Section fields: id, title, and summary are the only required fields. The domain model: a template is a Section with no source.

name: version-only
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: the loader does not validate, so a file with only schemaVersion gives the zero Section. The section validator reports the missing id, title, and summary.

name: all-fields
source: Hand-written. Every field of the domain model Section, Variable, Condition, Clause, AnswerTest, Step, and Check that a template can hold, in a key order that is not the canonical one. Section template schema, variables.md, conditions.md, steps.md, escalation.md, optional-sections.md. The section clauses follow the decoder contract, Section clauses: both keys, either order, and an empty section read as the empty string. A variable may hold example, in any key order, and it is a text field like description, never the default.

name: unvalidated
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: What passes through. Validating is the section validator's job (components doc). An unknown type, a bad name, a reserved id, a variable named enabled, a reserved name (0050), with a default of Deferred, two steps with one id, a check with two keys, an includeIf on a section question, and an empty condition pass unchanged.

name: placeholders
source: Hand-written. variables.md, Syntax and Dollar signs: $name and $$ are plain text in the file and stay unresolved. steps.md: a command variable is written run: [$name], a list of one item holding the text $name. An example keeps its dollar signs as written, like a description.

name: deferred
source: Hand-written. variables.md, Deferred answers, and the decoder contract, Values: the plain word is Deferred only as a whole plain Value. In a string field and in a list of strings it is text, and quoted it is text.

name: null-and-empty
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Known fields: a null or absent field is the zero value, a present includeIf or askIf is a Condition even when empty, an unset isSettled stays unset, a null env value is the empty string, and an env map that is present is not nil. An empty list of values is nil, and an empty list as a Value is a List with no items. A null, empty, or quoted empty example is the empty string.

name: strings
source: Hand-written. 0030 Format: quote what would read as a boolean, a number, or null. Decoder contract, Scalars: quoted and block scalars are always text, and a plain date, nULL, 12ab, v1.0, 12:30:45, and 1,000 are text. A quoted string keeps its leading and trailing spaces. A variable example is text like a description: quoted or plain, a quoted yes, a plain date, 1,000, v1.0, and padded spaces are kept, and a variable may hold an example and no description.

name: style-is-free
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Style is free: comments, a leading document marker, a quoted key, flow style, single and double quotes, folded and literal blocks with chomping, and any key order.

name: list-order
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Known fields: a list keeps its items in file order and keeps repeats. Section template schema, ordering.md: order is computed later, never by the loader.

name: empty-file
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-a-template. An empty file is not a template.

name: comments-only
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: a file of only comments is empty.

name: root-list
source: Hand-written. A template file is one section, so a list of sections is not a template. Contract rule: Problems, file.not-a-template.

name: not-yaml
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: file.not-yaml.

name: invalid-utf8
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: the bytes must be UTF-8.

name: multiple-documents
source: Hand-written. A template file is one section, so a second document is a problem. Decoder contract, Problems: file.multiple-documents.

name: parse-error-in-second-document
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: a syntax error in any document wins over the second-document problem.

name: version-missing
source: Hand-written. 0030 Versioning: schemaVersion is on template files. Contract rule: Version. A template with no schemaVersion is refused.

name: version-quoted
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Version: a quoted version is not a canonical integer.

name: version-decimal
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Version: a decimal is not a canonical integer.

name: version-zero
source: Hand-written. 0030 Versioning: older than supported is refused. Decoder contract, Version.

name: version-too-new-with-other-problems
source: Hand-written. 0030 Versioning: a newer file is refused and nothing else is read, so its unknown keys, its source key, its yes, and its wrong types are not reported.

name: duplicate-version
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Version: two schemaVersion keys are a duplicate key and the only problem.

name: boolean-spelling
source: Hand-written. 0030 Format: an unquoted yes, no, on, off, y, n, True, or TRUE is an error, so a hand-edited required: yes is a problem and not a silent true. Spelling is checked before type, in a string field, a boolean field, a Value, a list item, and a map value. An example is a string field, so a plain Off in it is a spelling problem.

name: number-spelling
source: Hand-written. 0030 Format: numbers that parse surprisingly, such as 1.0 or a leading zero, are errors where a string is meant. Decoder contract, Numbers: the list of spellings, and a canonical number where a string or a Value is read. An example is a string field, so a canonical decimal in it is a spelling problem.

name: null-spelling
source: Hand-written. 0030 Format: null is null or an omitted key. Decoder contract, Scalars: ~, Null, and NULL are problems. null and nULL are not. An example is a string field, so a ~ in it is the null spelling.

name: alias
source: Hand-written. 0030 Format: anchors and aliases are rejected. Decoder contract, Problems: a merge key is one problem at the key, and its value is not read.

name: duplicate-key
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: format.duplicate-key. Each key after the first is reported, and a quoted key is the same key as a plain one.

name: wrong-type
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: format.wrong-type, from the domain model's type of each field. A scalar run is a wrong type in a step and in a check, so run: git status, run: $Upper, and a check's run: $cmd are wrong types. A map or list in a value of the wrong type is not read.

name: null-items
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: format.empty-item for a null in a list, and format.empty-answer for a null in isOneOf or isNotOneOf, because dropping either would shift the list.

name: unknown-field-top
source: Hand-written. 0030 Format and Versioning: templates reject unknown fields, most often a typo. Unlike a plan, a template keeps no x- key and no key of another case. The value of an unknown key is not read, so the yes in author is not reported. The quoted key "<<" is an ordinary key, so here it is unknown.

name: unknown-field-everywhere
source: Hand-written. 0030 Format: templates decode strictly. An unknown key is a problem in a condition, a clause, an answer test, a variable, a step, and a check, and schemaVersion is known only at the top.

name: source-key
source: Hand-written. Section template schema, Section fields: source is plan only. 0030 Identifiers: authors never write a hash into a template file. A template has no source, so the key is unknown.

name: unknown-field-repeated
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Unknown fields: every unknown key is reported, a repeated one each time together with the duplicate. The value of an unknown key is not read.

name: plan-as-template
source: Hand-written. 0030: a plan holds sections and a template is one section. The plan's variables key is also a section field, so it is read. provenance, answers, and sections are unknown to a template.

name: many-problems
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: all problems are reported, in the order of the file. The value of the unknown x-ext is not read, so its 0x10 is not reported.

name: same-place
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Problems: two problems at one place come in the order of its table, the spelling and then the anchor.

name: wrong-type-values
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Values and Problems: a map, or a list holding a list or a map, is not a Value, and the problem is at the list item that is not text, and a list or map where a boolean or a string belongs is a wrong type. Nothing inside a value of the wrong type is read, so the yes and the 1.0 in them are not reported. An example that is a list or a map, or a plain true, is a wrong type, as a description is, and nothing inside it is read.

name: tags
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Style is free: a tag is ignored, and a scalar is read by its text and its style alone, so !!str yes is still the spelling yes.

name: complex-key
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Style is free: a key that is not a scalar is a wrong type, at the path of the map that holds it. The entries after it are still read.

name: run-scalar
source: Hand-written. Decided by a person: run is always a list. steps.md writes a command variable as run: [$test_command]. A scalar run is a wrong type at the field, in a step and in a check, whether it is plain text, a plain $name, or a quoted $name.

name: section-clauses
source: Hand-written. Decoder contract, Section clauses: a clause with a section key is a section clause, in either key order and in flow or block style, and an empty or null section is read as the empty string. 0050 Decision, and conditions.md. A section clause is read in includeIf and in askIf. The loader does not check the id.

name: section-clause-mixed
source: Hand-written from the decoder contract, Section clauses, and its cases clause-forms and clause-missing-enabled. A clause with a section key is a section clause, so its question and answer are format.unknown-field at the key and are not read: the list, the plain yes, and the null are not reported. Without a section key, enabled is an unknown key of a question clause and its value is not read. A key counts as the other form even when its value is null. At the one place of the clause and its first key, format.wrong-type comes before format.unknown-field. Valid clauses in between are read.

name: section-clause-wrong-type
source: Hand-written from the decoder contract, Section clauses, Known fields, and Problems, and its cases enabled-wrong-type, enabled-spelling, and clause-missing-enabled. enabled is a boolean with the spelling guard and section is text. A quoted true, a canonical number, a list, and a map are format.wrong-type where a boolean belongs, and a plain true is wrong where text belongs. A section clause whose enabled is absent, empty, or null is format.wrong-type at the clause, and a ~ is the null spelling alone. A clause problem comes before a problem at the clause's first key with the same code. Any other key is format.unknown-field.

name: template-enabled-key
source: Hand-written. 0050: a template never declares the section switch and a template section has no enabled. The key is unknown on the template, a variable, a step, and a check, as any unknown key is, and its plain yes is not read.

name: wrong-type-items
source: Hand-written from the decoder contract, Problems: format.wrong-type, and its case wrong-type-items. A plain text where a condition clause or an answer test belongs is a wrong type at the item or at answer, in includeIf and in askIf, and the loader goes on without it. A list where a clause or an answer test belongs is the same wrong kind. A plain text where all belongs is a wrong type at all. The section clause after them is read.
